body: The spec's load-bearing assumption is empirically unverified and likely false: the HCP 1200 Subjects release contains no Music Task and no Music Emotion Rating behavioral data. The original project description correctly sourced behavioral scores externally (Barcelona Music Reward Questionnaire, Mas-Herrero et al., 2014), but this spec repeatedly asserts a paired 'HCP Music Task subset' exists (US-1, FR-001, Assumptions). If MER scores must be joined from an external dataset, subject overlap with HCP is not established anywhere here — the merge in US-2 presupposes an intersection whose size is unknown and could plausibly be near zero. SC-005's power requirement (detecting r ≥ 0.20 at power ≥ 0.80, i.e., N ≈ 194) cannot be evaluated until this intersection is quantified; the spec defers it but builds every downstream requirement on the assumption it will be met. Two further technical issues: (1) fMRIPrep does not perform bandpass filtering — it explicitly leaves temporal filtering to downstream tools — so US-1 scenario 2 and FR-002 conflate fMRIPrep's outputs with confound-regression steps it does not provide; (2) HCP resting-state data is distributed already minimally preprocessed (fix pipelines), so re-running fMRIPrep on it is at best redundant and at worst methodologically inappropriate. Finally, running fMRIPrep on even a modest subset within a 6-hour, 7 GB GitHub Actions runner (SC-004) is not a feasibility assumption to wave through — a single subject's CPU-only run can take hours; the spec should state the per-subject runtime budget explicitly or restrict to the distributed preprocessed data.
